item.title: PyTorch 2.15 Enhancements for Metal Performance Shaders on Mac
item.description:
PyTorch 2.15 Enhancements for Metal Performance Shaders on Mac

PyTorch 2.15 introduces significant performance and memory optimizations for Apple silicon Macs via Metal Performance Shaders (MPS), specifically targeting Large Language Model (LLM) decoding, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, and video processing.

💡 Why it matters

Performance gains are most evident in MoE models, which decode 5–6.5× faster than in version 2.14. For example, on an M3 Ultra using torch.compile:

Model 2.14 Speed PyTorch 2.15 Speed
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 9.4 tokens/s 61.3 tokens/s
LFM2.5-8B-A1B 23.6 tokens/s 123.6 tokens/s

🧩 How it works

  • FP8 Support: PyTorch 2.15 adds torch.float8_e4m3fn tensors on MPS. These use one byte per value, requiring half the storage of BF16 or FP16. Tensors can be multiplied directly on the GPU using F.scaled_mm, which supports rowwise and tensorwise scaling.
  • MoE Optimizations: New Metal kernels read group offsets directly on the GPU using Metal Performance Primitives or a separate Metal path, replacing the 2.14 method of copying offsets to the CPU. A dedicated decoding path and specialized kernels for small groups further reduce GPU-CPU syncs and improve top-k routing.
  • Linear Layer Improvements: F.linear now connects to GEMV kernels for common [1, 1, hidden_size] decoding inputs with fused bias additions. This resulted in a 1.23× geometric-mean speedup across 96 BF16 layer shapes from real models.
  • General GPU Acceleration: Softmax over the vocabulary is approximately 8× faster, and there is increased GPU support for complex LU and triangular solves, QR decomposition, and small-matrix inverses.

⚙️ Key details

  • Video and Audio: Faster paths are available for reductions, interpolation backward, dropout, padding, convolutions, and audio/video training.
  • Memory Efficiency: Wan2.2’s tiled VAE video decode memory peak has been reduced from 270 GiB to approximately 8 GiB.
  • Bug Fixes: A padding change fixes an issue where the Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE encoder corrupted images on MPS. Encode-decode round trips now match CPU at 29.95 dB PSNR, up from 10.06 dB.
  • Python Control: Users now have access to public MPS streams and more reliable event timing.

🚀 Availability

  • System Requirements: Apple silicon Mac running macOS 15 or later.
  • Software Requirements: PyTorch 2.15 requires Python 3.11 or later.
  • Diagnostics: The MPS availability check now specifies the reason if the OS is too old or no Metal GPU is available.

🔍 Looking Ahead

PyTorch 2.16 is expected to bring faster LLM decoding, more MPSGraph-to-Metal migrations, and attention fully implemented on Metal.

#PyTorch #AppleSilicon #Metal #LLM #MachineLearning

Source: MPS in PyTorch 2.15

item.title: Jun Kim Joins Hugging Face to Support oMLX and MLX Community
item.description:
Jun Kim Joins Hugging Face to Support oMLX and MLX Community

Jun Kim, the creator and maintainer of oMLX, has joined Hugging Face to support the MLX community. MLX is Apple’s framework for local AI, specifically optimized for Apple Silicon.

⚙️ Key details

  • oMLX Status: The project remains under the Apache 2.0 license, and Jun Kim continues to lead it.
  • Project Evolution: oMLX is transitioning from a side job to a fully maintained and funded project.
  • Objectives: The goal is to provide the tools and building blocks necessary to unblock the community from running local AI in any shape or form.

💡 Why it matters

  • Development Speed: Funding and maintenance are expected to provide stability and faster development, allowing Jun Kim to better guide contributors for the long-term.
  • Innovation: oMLX is expected to serve as a testbed for new ideas while leveraging dependencies such as mlx-lm and mlx-vlm.
  • Streamlining Models: A primary focus is the quick transition from a transformers model definition to a reference MLX implementation. Since the transformers library is the reference for ML model definitions, this aims to streamline making new transformers models run on MLX.
  • Collaboration: Hugging Face intends to strengthen relationships with teams including those of Cheng, Prince, and Yagil, as well as projects like LMStudio, mlx-lm, and mlx-vlm.

#MLX #oMLX #HuggingFace #AppleSilicon #LocalAI

Source: Jun Kim, oMLX creator and maintainer, joins Hugging Face to support the MLX community

item.title: Transformers Now Supports llama.cpp GGUF Quantizations for Local Inference
item.description:
Transformers Now Supports llama.cpp GGUF Quantizations for Local Inference

The Transformers library now allows users to run llama.cpp GGUF quantizations using from_pretrained, enabling AI model generation directly on a user’s own machine.

🔍 Overview

GGUF is a widely used format for local inference developed by the llama.cpp team. It packages model weights and metadata—including tokenizer information and optional chat templates—into a single file. This format supports various quantization levels, allowing users to reduce the memory footprint by trading off some precision.

🧩 How it works

To achieve performance close to llama.cpp, Transformers reuses its underlying ggml kernels through the kernels library and reduces overhead in generate.

  • Loading: Users pass the Hub model_id and filename as gguf_file to from_pretrained.
  • Execution: On Apple Silicon, when weights stay packed on Metal, Transformers automatically loads compatible ggml/Metal layer kernels and uses ggml-org/ggml-attn for attention implementation.
  • Fallbacks: If the compatible kernel cannot be fetched, the system falls back to “sdpa” (which can also be forced by passing attn_implementation="sdpa"). Without a compatible quantization kernel, the loader dequantizes the model, which uses more memory.

⚙️ Key details

Initial focus is on local inference for Apple Silicon, starting with the Qwen3.5 architecture. Users can select different quantization variants based on their available memory:

Quantization Variant Description
Q4_K_M Mixes tensor precisions; uses mostly 4-bit weights while keeping sensitive tensors at higher precision.
Q5_K_M Recommended for users with more memory available.
Q6_K Recommended for users with more memory available.

🚀 Availability

Ready-to-use GGUF checkpoints are available on the Hub from several providers:

  • ggml-org
  • Unsloth
  • LM Studio Community
  • bartowski

💡 Why it matters

Running AI models locally has been made practical through llama.cpp and projects like MLX. The llama.cpp inference engine already powers tools such as Ollama, Jan, and LM Studio. Integrating this into Transformers makes it easier to run these models locally while allowing the same endpoint to be used by other clients that support the API.

#Transformers #llama.cpp #GGUF #LocalAI #AppleSilicon

Source: Transformers now runs llama.cpp quants

item.title: Perplexity Launches Hybrid Compute and Lily Inference Engine for Mac
item.description:
Perplexity Launches Hybrid Compute and Lily Inference Engine for Mac

Perplexity has introduced hybrid compute for its Mac app, allowing a single Perplexity Computer task to be split between cloud-based frontier models and a compact local model.

🧩 How it works

Tasks begin in the cloud for reasoning, planning, and search. Sensitive steps are then handed down to the Mac without losing context or restarting. This process is managed by an on-device privacy gate that determines if data should be:

  • Kept local
  • Masked
  • Refused
  • Asked for consent

⚙️ Key details

Perplexity has open-sourced two components related to this development:

Component Description
0.6B Classifier The model behind the privacy gate, recording the highest character F1 (0.629) among twelve evaluated detectors.
Lily A local inference engine built in Rust with custom Metal kernels for one model on one chip family.

On a 40-core, 128 GB M5 Max, Lily averages 1.35x the decode throughput and 1.23x the prefill throughput of MLX-LM.

🚀 Availability

Hybrid compute is currently live for the following users:

  • Pro
  • Max
  • Enterprise

It requires Apple silicon Macs with 24GB of unified memory.

#Perplexity #HybridCompute #LocalAI #AppleSilicon #OpenSource

Source: Asif Razzaq
